name: Consensus
summary: AI search across peer-reviewed literature: it reports what published studies found, not whether those studies are sound. Study quality and conflicting results still need your own judgment.
best_for: researchers, clinicians, students and writers who want evidence-backed answers drawn from peer-reviewed papers instead of the open web
skip_if: your questions are practical/commercial rather than research-based (a general AI assistant fits), or you need full systematic-review rigor (this accelerates it, not replaces it)
honest_knock: It searches peer-reviewed literature, which is its strength and its boundary: it can tell you what published studies found, not whether those studies are good. Study quality, sample sizes and conflicting results still need your judgment, and the AI summary layer can smooth over genuine scientific disagreement. Treat it as a dramatically faster literature scan, not an oracle; click through to the papers that matter. Consensus's own developer notes (read 21 October 2026) add three limits worth knowing before you pay. The corpus is English-first: non-English papers are indexed where metadata exists, but ranking and summaries are tuned for English. It is not a news feed: papers published in the last few weeks may not be indexed yet. And the Consensus Meter is described as a heuristic, not a formal meta-analysis.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month, billed annually ($20 billed monthly)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 28 September 2026 in a rendered browser, monthly and annual tabs) Free: $0, 10 Pro messages and up to 3 Deep reviews a month. Pro: $20 a month billed monthly, or $12 a month billed annually ($144 a year), with unlimited Pro messages, 15 Deep reviews a month and 500 API and MCP uses included, then $0.05 a use up to 1,000. Deep: $65 monthly, or $45 a month billed annually ($540 a year), with 200 Deep reviews and 2,000 API and MCP uses, then $0.05 a use up to 10,000. Students and faculty with a school email and US healthcare professionals with an NPI number can get up to 40% off. Team and Enterprise carry no amount on the page; the vendor's machine-readable pricing file puts Team at up to 200 seats with 50 Deep searches per seat and Enterprise on contract, and on 28 September it still gave Free 15 Pro messages where the rendered page said 10; re-read on 21 October 2026, that file has been aligned at 10 Pro messages and 3 Deep Searches a month, and it describes the student discount as 40% off for 12 months with a verified .edu or student email. The unit that matters is Deep reviews rather than seats. Correction: our earlier reading, which we could not confirm at the time, put Pro at about $15 a month or roughly $10 annually. The paid amounts are rendered in the browser from Stripe and could not be re-read on 21 October 2026 without one, so the dollar figures above still date from 28 September.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We asked one research question, read the answer and its sources, opened the export options and the bibliography view, and read the plan and checkout screens. We stopped before payment. This is a literature search engine, so the import kit does not apply.
findings: The sidebar showed '10 / 10 Pro messages left'. One question used one Pro message and the counter read 9 / 10.

Question: 'Does regular physical activity reduce the risk of depression in adults?' The answer said yes, with a 17% to 25% lower risk. The Consensus Meter, based on 19 papers, showed Yes 100%. A note says it 'may not be a perfect reflection of the current science'.
We checked the top source (Pearce et al., JAMA Psychiatry, 2022) and it matches the published paper. Other cited papers also exist. One sentence repeated a citation twice.

Export offers the 18 cited papers by default, the top 20, or all 49 papers on Pro. Formats are CSV, RIS and a bibliography in APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, BibTeX and AMA. The APA view had formatting slips: doubled full stops after titles, a space before a final full stop and a journal name not in title case.
The upgrade screen preselects Annual. Pro is $12 a month billed yearly ($144) or $20 monthly. The Free column says 'without any AI analysis' and lists 10 Pro messages a month in the same column.
Monthly Pro checkout read EUR 18.61 for the Netherlands, with annual billing offered at EUR 133.98 a year. No VAT line showed before card entry.

Accuracy beyond the one question and the sources we checked
